verdicts.proposal_name: Proposal 1: Procyclical credit supply, zeta(x), with tau and kappa_b recalibration
verdicts.critique:
Three referee-fatal problems, one of which the proposer did not detect.

(1) THE PARAMETER BEING MADE STOCHASTIC IS ALREADY INCONSISTENT BETWEEN SOLVE AND SIMULATION. I read utils_gs21/GS21.m line 35: `xi = 0.03/3*3;` = 0.03. config.py:296 sets GS21_ZETA = 0.03/3 = 0.01, and that is what utils_gs21/sdf_compute_gs21.py:132,157-168,177,184 and utils_gs21/panel_functions_gs21.py:49,200-201 all use. So the value function was solved under a refinancing intensity three times the one the panel simulates and the one the conditional second moment integrates against. Proposal 1's entire mechanism is the derivative of value with respect to this parameter. You cannot make a parameter stochastic and priced when the solve and the simulation currently disagree about its level by 3x. Fix the level first, re-run the baseline, and see how much of the existing 0.5112 vs 0.4433 DKKM/FF gap survives.

(2) THE SPAN ARGUMENT CONFLATES "ZERO LINEAR PROJECTION ON A CHARACTERISTIC" WITH "UNSPANNED BY THE LINEAR PORTFOLIOS." These are different claims and only the first is proved. The proposal's verified fact -- linear R^2 of exp(-c|u|) is 0.000 -- establishes that no single char portfolio has a cross-sectional tilt correlated with beta_credit. It does NOT establish that the 7-portfolio linear span cannot attain the required factor exposure. G_i = P_up - P_down >= 0 with equality only at the vertex, so the equal-weighted market portfolio (fama_functions.fama_macbeth line ~175, P['mkt_rf'] = 1/len(d)) has E[beta_credit] > 0 mechanically. With two priced factors and seven linear portfolios, the exposure-matching problem is over-determined; the linear span hits both loadings and forfeits only the O(1/N) diversification residual. This is precisely what the project's own span2.py measured: under exact factor pricing every basis including equal-weight lands within 0.6% of SR*, and adding a 20x spread in d changed nothing. Proposal 1 keeps the economy an exact factor model. Its headline prediction that linear-6 falls from 0.871 to 0.20-0.30 of max SR^2 is, on the evidence already in this project, off by roughly a factor of three.

(3) BUNDLING. The tau change (0.2/3 -> 0.20) is a genuine units-bug fix and is defensible on its own. The kappa_b change (0.004 -> 0.02, 5x) is a free parameter moved in exactly the direction that widens the inaction region and hence the effect. Bundling a bug fix with an effect-amplifying free-parameter move in one commit is how a referee decides the authors searched.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: FF and FM can capture most of it and I expect they will. beta_credit is weakly positive for every firm, so the market/equal-weight column already delivers the credit-factor exposure; FM has seven columns to hit two factor targets. What the linear span genuinely cannot form is the D^{-1} tilt on a V-shaped numerator, w* ~ (V_i/d_i), and in GS21 that tilt is worth 0.19% of SR* at N=1000 per the project's own measurement -- unless d_i is made hugely dispersed, which is Proposal 4/5's job, not this one. Even granting the full amplitude story (sd(G/P) 0.0024 -> 0.007), the new premium component is a smooth, symmetric, low-order function of ONE index; the diagnosis measured the entire quadratic headroom in GS21 at 0.871 -> 0.909 of max SR^2. A degree-2 basis buys 4 points of SR^2. FM re-estimated monthly on rank chars is not far off a degree-2 basis once mkt_lev is repaired (Proposal 2), because a symmetric V in a bounded rank variable is 74-88% quadratic and FM sees mkt_lev and book_lev separately. Realistic outcome: DKKM/FM goes from 1.03 to perhaps 1.10-1.25, not 1.7-1.9.
verdicts.salvage: Keep the two disclosed bug fixes and drop the rest for now. (a) Reconcile ZETA between GS21.m line 35 and config.py:296 and re-run the baseline -- this is mandatory regardless. (b) Fix tau = 0.20; dividing a marginal tax rate by 3 is unambiguously a units error and needs no defense. Then, before writing a single line of the zeta(x) code, compute the ORACLE span ratio at the corrected calibration: per month, SR_lin = sqrt(mu' X (X' Sigma X)^{-1} X' mu) with X = [1, chars] versus SR_rff with the configured RFF, using the rp and cond_var already in the moments pickle. If the oracle ratio does not clear 1.5 the proposal is dead and no amount of estimation-side work will revive it. Report that number in the paper whatever it is.

verdicts.proposal_name: Proposal 2: Repair mkt_lev and add book_lev, distance-to-default, rolling investment rate, and cash-flow volatility
verdicts.critique:
The core claim is correct and I verified it. utils_gs21/panel_functions_gs21.py:278 is `df["mkt_lev"] = df["book_lev"] * df["bm"]`, book_lev is `debt` (the coupon per unit capital, line 243), and bm = book/mve = 1/P_ex, so mkt_lev = b/P_ex -- coupon over equity, not market leverage. Q_0 is already constructed as a RegularGridInterpolator at utils_gs21/sdf_compute_gs21.py:69 and is in scope in panel_functions_gs21.py via the star-import at line 15. So the fix is available and cheap, and the prior conclusion that "GS21 firms are effectively all-equity" was an artifact of a mis-defined characteristic rather than a property of the model. That is a real correction and it must ship.

My referee objections are about how it is presented and what it is claimed to buy.

(a) DISCLOSURE. This is a bug fix in a characteristic that is one of only six inputs and the only one distinguishing GS21 from the default char set (config.py:223). It must appear in the paper as a correction with the before/after table, not silently in a revised results section. If a reader later diffs the repo and finds mkt_lev changed from 0.0013 to 0.32 between drafts with no note, that is the end of the paper's credibility.

(b) IT IS SYMMETRIC AND MAY NARROW THE GAP. The proposal says this honestly, and I want to reinforce it: FM gets four more linear regressors and its pinvh conditioning improves because mkt_lev is no longer three orders of magnitude smaller than log size (fama_functions.fama_macbeth uses RAW unstandardized chars, lines ~158-161, standardization commented out). Repairing mkt_lev strengthens the linear benchmark. That is the right thing to do and it makes the eventual DKKM result more credible, but it is not a step toward the target.

(c) DISTANCE-TO-DEFAULT IS DEAD AND SHOULD NOT SHIP YET. z_cut_down is pinned at the zgrid floor at every (x,b) in the shipped solfiles, so dd is an affine transform of z and duplicates roe. Shipping a characteristic that is by construction a copy of another characteristic, and only becomes informative after a separate proposal lands, invites the objection that the char set was expanded to pad the RFF input dimension. Gate it on Proposal 5.

(d) THE MECHANICAL HANDICAP TO THE LINEAR METHODS IS REAL. Going from K=7 to K=11 raises the FF/FM plug-in Sharpe loss from ~2K/T = 3.9% to 6.1%, while DKKM's ridge absorbs the extra dimension for free. It is a 2-point handicap, small but it runs in the paper's favored direction and a referee will notice. Report both char sets for the linear methods.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No, and the proposer says so. The one asymmetric channel claimed -- cfvol as a noisy proxy that requires a nonlinear shrinkage map -- is real in principle but its magnitude is a free choice (36 vs 24 months), and FM's unpenalized OLS is the wrong comparison because the honest fix is to give FM a ridge grid too, at which point FM can shrink on the noisy proxy exactly as well. The effective-rank argument (20.7 at L=6 to 38.5 at L=10) is also weaker than it sounds: T = 360, so effective c goes from 0.058 to 0.107. DKKM's virtue-of-complexity regime needs effective c above 1, i.e. L on the order of 50. Ten characteristics is not a step change in the quantity DKKM's Theorem 3 is stated on; it is a 1.9x move within the classical regime.
verdicts.salvage: Ship the mkt_lev repair and book_lev immediately, as a standalone commit labelled a bug fix, and re-run the full baseline before touching anything else -- everyone needs to know what the corrected baseline DKKM/FF and DKKM/FM numbers are. Add ivest (it genuinely de-degenerates the cma sort, which currently sorts a variable that is 0 in 98.8% of firm-months) and cfvol with the window pre-registered at 36 months and never revisited. Hold dd. Report the linear methods at both the 6-char and the enlarged char set so the K-inflation handicap is visible.

verdicts.proposal_name: Proposal 3: Restore sigma_z to the paper calibration, raise rho_z to 0.985, and repair the solve-vs-simulation parameter mismatches
verdicts.critique:
The mismatch claim is correct and worse than the proposal states. I checked the shipped grids directly against three candidate parameterizations:

  zgrid.max() = 0.146826069677159. 4 x stationary sd of 0.1*0.16*sqrt((1-0.9^(2/3))/(1-0.9^2)) = 0.146826069677159. Exact match to 15 digits.
  xgrid.max() = 0.153723027652884. 4 x stationary sd of 0.012*sqrt((1-0.95^(2/3))/(1-0.95^2)) = 0.153723027652884. Exact match.

config.py:287 and :290 use the (3/2) exponent, giving sigma_x = 0.010458 and sigma_z = 0.014034, i.e. 1.484x and 1.468x the values the value function was solved for. The interpolators are built with fill_value=None (sdf_compute_gs21.py:61-74), so off-grid draws are silently linearly extrapolated with no warning and no counter. This is a defect in the CURRENT published baseline, not in any proposal, and it must be fixed before any result from this model is reportable.

And it is a three-way disagreement, not a two-way. GS21.m line 25 has sigma_z with NO 0.1 factor (0.0956); the solfiles were solved WITH the 0.1 factor; config.py has the 0.1 factor but the wrong exponent. Likewise GS21.m:27 r = 0.1/12 versus config.py:299 r = 0.074830/12, and GS21.m:35 xi = 0.03 versus config.py:296 zeta = 0.01. The GS21.m in the repository does not generate the solfiles in the repository, and tauchen.m and gaussHermite.m (called at GS21.m:73-74 and :57) are not present anywhere on disk.

My objections to the proposal as written:

(a) rho_z = 0.985 IS NOT A FIX, IT IS A NEW CALIBRATION. GS21's rho_z = 0.9^(1/3) is the paper's parameter. Changing it to 0.985 is defended by Foster-Haltiwanger-Syverson and Fama-French, which is a respectable citation, but it is the first genuinely discretionary move in this list and it happens to be the one that multiplies d log P / d z by the duration ratio, i.e. the one that makes the cross-section move. Separate it from the sigma restoration and report both.

(b) THE Z-GRID PROBLEM IS NOT A DETAIL. Restoring sigma_z 10x AND raising rho_z to 0.985 takes stationary sd(z) from 0.0539 to 0.554 -- the grid must widen 15x. At znum = 200 that is a 15x coarser mesh through exactly the region where the value function is most curved. The proposal acknowledges the 576 GB alternative. This is the item that determines whether the whole program is feasible.

(c) HONESTY CREDIT. The proposal states plainly that the standalone DKKM/FM effect is 1.03 -> 1.05-1.15 and that a monotone heteroskedasticity channel hands FM 76-92% of itself. That is the correct framing and I would accept it in a paper.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: No, and correctly so -- the proposal calls itself an enabler. The adversarial point worth pressing is that it may hurt the headline: the proposal itself predicts max_sr falls from 0.438/month to 0.15-0.25/month, because GS21's current Sharpe is largely a sqrt(N) near-arbitrage manufactured by 2%/month idiosyncratic volatility. That is scientifically the right direction, but it means every level in the tables drops by half and the paper must switch to reporting Sharpe/SR* (the Sigma-cosine). If the authors restore sigma_z and then quietly keep reporting raw Sharpes, a referee comparing drafts will see the numbers collapse and ask why. Also: 76-92% of a monotone inverse-variance channel goes to FM, and the interaction channel the proposal reserves for DKKM (d_i = f(book_lev, roe) x g(x_t)) is a date-level multiplier g(x_t) that NO method's feature map sees -- dkkm_functions.rff appends rf only for model=='bgn', so GS21's RFF has no time-varying input at all, and the ridge coefficient is a single vector over 360 months. DKKM cannot exploit g(x_t) any more than FM can.
verdicts.salvage: Split into three commits and report the baseline after each. (1) Fix the (3/2) vs (2/3) exponent in config.py:287 and :290 so the simulation matches the grid the value function was actually solved on, and reconcile r and zeta. Add an explicit off-grid counter to the simulation so this class of error cannot recur silently. This commit changes nothing economically and is pure hygiene; it must be in the paper's appendix. (2) Restore sigma_z to the model's own documented value (drop the 0.1 factor added on 2026-06-09 in commits eee2386/dc2462e) and re-solve. This is a revert of an undisclosed ad hoc change and needs only the sentence "we use the calibration in Gomes-Schmid (2021)." (3) Treat rho_z = 0.985 as a separate, clearly labelled recalibration with its own robustness column at rho_z = 0.9^(1/3). Do not fold it into (2).

verdicts.proposal_name: Proposal 4: Five permanent industry types with different sigma_z
verdicts.critique:
The economics is unobjectionable -- industry cash-flow volatility heterogeneity is real and GS21's single sigma_z is its least defensible homogeneity assumption. My objection is entirely about how the proposal is specified, and it is specified in a way that would not survive a referee report.

(a) THE PROPOSAL CONTAINS ITS OWN TUNING LOOP, IN WRITING. Two sentences: "if it comes out too wide, cut kappa to ln(3.5)/2.564 = 0.489" and "if the linear R^2 exceeds ~0.85 the channel is inert and either kappa or the window must change (shorten to 24 months to raise the proxy noise to 14.4%)." Those are instructions to adjust a structural parameter and an econometrician-side measurement window until the DKKM-favorable channel is live. If any version of that appears in the replication package or the commit history, a referee will quote it and the paper is done. The kappa target (10-90 ratio of 5.0, from Ang-Hodrick-Xing-Zhang) is a legitimate calibration target; the fallback is not.

(b) THE CLAIMED DKKM EDGE IS AN ESTIMATOR ARTIFACT, NOT ECONOMICS. The three asymmetric channels are: the ratio book_lev/b*(cfvol), the moving vertex, and "the optimal weight is E[1/sigma_z | cfvol_observed], a nonlinear SHRINKAGE map, and FM's unpenalized OLS (ALPHA_LST_FAMA = [0], config.py:187) cannot represent a shrinkage map." The proposal calls point (c) "the cleanest formal argument." It is the weakest, because it is an artifact of the referee-fairness defect that runs through this entire project: FF and FM are handed alpha = 0 and DKKM is handed six alphas whose winner is selected post hoc on the evaluation metric (create_slides_tables.find_best_alpha_for_model, lines 81-97, returns max over alphas of the mean Sharpe across iterations). Give FM the same ridge grid and it represents the shrinkage map perfectly well. Building a proposal on FM's lack of regularization is building on plumbing.

(c) PERMANENT TYPES ARE LEARNABLE. Fixed effects over a 360-month rolling window are recovered almost exactly by any method, including FM, which re-runs the cross-sectional regression each month with cfvol as a regressor. The proposal notes this risk itself and suggests slow Markov migration, which would be the right specification.

(d) FIVE SETS OF SOLFILES multiplies an already irreproducible solve by five. GS21.m does not currently regenerate one set (see my Proposal 3 verdict); five is five times unreproducible.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: FM captures most of it, by the proposal's own arithmetic: linear R^2 of exp(-c u) is 0.861 at a 25x variance range. The residual is a two-characteristic multiplicative term at linear R^2 = 0.458 vs quadratic 0.815 -- which means a QUADRATIC basis, not a 3600-feature RFF, gets nearly all of the remainder. That maps onto the diagnosis's measured GS21 span numbers exactly: linear-6 = 0.871, +21 quadratics = 0.909, RFF360 = 0.988. Adding heteroskedasticity moves premium into a channel where the quadratic basis is already 91% of the way there. And the deeper problem is the one from Proposal 1: dispersion in d only matters through the inverse-variance tilt, and under exact factor pricing with N = 1000 that tilt is worth 0.19% of SR*. The project's own span2.py measured SR* = 0.100, linear span = 0.100 with d spanning 20x. Heteroskedastic D is a multiplier on an unspanned alpha, and this proposal adds no alpha. On its own I would expect DKKM/FM to move from 1.03 to 1.08-1.12, consistent with the proposal's own 1.10-1.15 estimate, which is a fifth of the target.
verdicts.salvage: Keep the economics, delete the discretion. Fix kappa = ln(5)/2.564 = 0.6277 from AHXZ and never touch it; if the realized idio-vol range comes out wrong, report that as a model failure rather than adjusting. Replace permanent types with a slow Markov industry-migration chain so the type is not a learnable fixed effect. Fix the cfvol window at 36 months by pre-registration. And critically: run the reformed-fairness comparison (FM and FF with the identical ridge grid and the identical post-hoc alpha selection DKKM gets) BEFORE claiming that the nonlinear shrinkage map is a DKKM-only capability -- I do not believe it is.

verdicts.proposal_name: Proposal 5: Turn on kappa_e, raise tau and bmax so the negative-cash-flow region and the default boundary are reachable, and simulate the sigma_m valuation shock
verdicts.critique:
This is the proposal with the best economics-to-plumbing ratio in the set and the only one whose defense in a referee report is a single clean sentence: "the model already contains these frictions; we turn them on at empirically standard values." I verified the code paths exist and are inert: GS21.m lines 253-254 and 259-260 are `P0_up_R = (1 + (prof0_up<=0).*kappa_e).*prof0_up` and the PI_up analogue, with kappa_e = 0 at line 33 and the intended 0.025 commented out; the sigma_m Gauss-Hermite default smoothing is at lines 53-59 and the perturbed price expectations at 263-264. panel_functions_gs21.py:72 tests P[t] <= 0 with no nu draw, so the simulation and the solve currently disagree about whether the default indicator is smoothed at all. That internal inconsistency is a genuine defect in the baseline and fixing it is not a model change.

Four objections.

(a) SIGMA_M IS THE PROBLEM. The proposal is right that sigma_m = 5 against P ~ 190 gives Phi(-38) = 0 exactly. But the fix it proposes -- "sigma_m must be chosen by a one-dimensional search on a simulated panel AFTER the re-solve" targeting 1%/yr defaults -- installs a pure numerical smoothing parameter, with no economic referent, as the direct control on how much nonlinearity the model has. A referee will read that as: the amount of the paper's headline effect is set by a free numerical constant tuned by search. Moody's 1.5%/yr is a legitimate target, so the search is defensible IF and only if the target is fixed in advance, disclosed, and the result is reported at 0.5%, 1%, and 2%/yr as a robustness triple. Without that triple I would reject on this point alone.

(b) THE MOVING-KINK ARGUMENT FOR DKKM IS WRONG. "The kink LOCATION depends on the aggregate state x_t... FM is re-estimated monthly so it can shift an intercept, but it cannot bend." DKKM cannot track a moving kink either. dkkm_functions.rff appends the raw rf column only for model == 'bgn'; GS21's RFF has no time-varying input, its features are purely cross-sectional rank transforms, and the ridge coefficient vector is estimated once per month on a 360-month window and applied to the whole cross-section. Both methods can shift a level and neither can move a kink. Drop this argument; the tail-location argument in point (a) of the proposal (linear R^2 of 1{u > p10} is 0.27 versus 0.75 at the median) is the good one and it stands on its own.

(c) SELECTIVE SAMPLE ATTRITION IS THE ROBUSTNESS CHECK I WOULD DEMAND FIRST. Defaulting firms reset with roe and mom NaN for 12 months (panel_functions_gs21.py:275,285) and prepare_panel drops them. So the very firms carrying the distress premium are systematically absent from the estimation sample for a year after every reset, and the attrition is correlated with the signal. At 1%/yr this is tolerable; if the calibration search lands at 3-5%/yr it is a first-order selection problem that biases every method, and it biases them differently because FF value-weights.

(d) IT IS CONDITIONAL ON PROPOSAL 3 AND PROBABLY DEAD WITHOUT IT. The proposal says so. Fine, but it means the paper cannot present this as an independent change.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: Partly, and it is the only proposal here for which I would concede that FF genuinely cannot compete: FF's 2x3 sorts value-weight (fama_functions.fama_french, the smb block at lines ~68-79 normalizes by mve), so the distressed small-cap tail where the kinks bind gets near-zero weight in every FF factor. A 2-3x DKKM/FF gap is plausible. But the FF comparison is the weak one -- the diagnosis already established that FM, a purely LINEAR method, closes 13 of the 16 points separating FF from the DKKM ceiling in GS21. Against FM the case is much thinner: default probability is convex but MONOTONE in distance-to-default, and once dd is supplied as a characteristic (Proposal 2) FM gets a lot of it -- the proposal's own number is linear R^2 = 0.763 even at a 100x range, and quadratic 0.971. A paper whose headline is "DKKM beats FF by 2.5x" while FM, with seven linear regressors, sits between them is not a virtue-of-complexity paper; it is a paper about the inefficiency of tercile sorting and value weighting. The referee's question will be: what is DKKM/FM? If the answer is 1.3, the abstract cannot say what the authors want it to say.
verdicts.salvage: Ship it, but with the presentation restructured around DKKM/FM rather than DKKM/FF, and with these commitments made before the re-solve: kappa_e = 0.05 (Hennessy-Whited) fixed; tau = 0.20 fixed as a units-bug fix; bmax set by the interest-coverage argument (b IS inverse coverage, so bmax = 2 gives coverage 0.5) and not by search; the default-rate target fixed at 1.5%/yr (Moody's all-corporate) and reported at 0.5/1.5/3.0 as a triple. Fix the two latent bugs in the replacement machinery first (panel_functions_gs21.py:85 never writes the redrawn xt back into x[t], and the while loop at line 73 has no iteration cap) -- they are dormant only because defaults never happen and both fire the moment this proposal lands. Remove the P_ex floor at line 131 and add an explicit minimum-eigenvalue guard on cond_var before scipy.linalg.solve, which at line 207 of sdf_compute_gs21.py is called on a module that is never imported.

verdicts.proposal_name: Proposal 6: An independent credit-conditions state s_t with its own price of risk gamma_s
verdicts.critique:
This is the most intellectually serious proposal and the one most likely to be read as "the authors added a factor until the answer came out." I would not reject it on identity grounds -- adding a stochastic external-finance state to a model whose defining friction is external finance is defensible and the He-Krishnamurthy / Gilchrist-Zakrajsek citation is the right one. I would reject it, as currently specified, on three other grounds.

(a) IT MAY SHRINK THE VERY QUANTITY DRIVING GS21'S SHARPE. The diagnosis measured that 89-97% of GS21's maximum squared Sharpe comes from the ALPHA leg -- the residual of mu on the single covariance loading, diversified across N nearly identical firms -- and only 3-11% from the market/beta leg. Adding a second priced factor moves premium from the alpha residual into the beta space, because more of mu is now explained by B. Mechanically, alpha' D^{-1} alpha falls. The proposal's prediction that the second eigenvalue rises from 0.03% to 5-20% of the first is probably right; the unstated consequence is that the alpha leg, which is what the linear span was failing to capture, gets smaller. The net effect on the DKKM/FM ratio is genuinely ambiguous and the proposal does not address it. This needs the oracle span calculation before any code is written.

(b) GAMMA_S IS FREE AND SET TO HIT A TARGET, AND THE PROPOSAL SHOWS ITS OWN ARITHMETIC FAILING. "At the CURRENT sd(G/P) = 0.00241 that is 1.1e-4, only 17% -- so this proposal MUST be combined with proposal 1's tau and kappa_b recalibration... To push the non-monotone share above 80% you need sd(G/P) ~ 0.03... which requires proposals 3 and 5 as well." Read that paragraph as a referee: the second factor is economically trivial at the model's own parameters, and reaching the target requires stacking four other changes each of which moves a free parameter in the same direction. That is a description of a search over a five-dimensional parameter space with the DKKM/FM ratio as the objective. It does not matter that each individual move has a citation attached; the joint move does not.

(c) IT IS NOT EXECUTABLE. Mmat at snum = 5 is 400,000 x 20,000 = 64 GB dense. tauchen.m and gaussHermite.m are absent from the repository (I checked: utils_gs21/ contains only GS21.m, GS21_solfiles/, and the Python files). GS21.m as posted does not reproduce the shipped solfiles -- it has sigma_z with no 0.1 factor and the (2/3) exponent, xi = 0.03 against config's 0.01, and r = 0.1/12 against config's 0.074830/12, while the shipped zgrid corresponds to a third parameterization (0.1 x 0.16 with the (2/3) exponent, matching zgrid.max() = 0.146826069677159 to 15 digits). Proposing a four-dimensional state space on top of a solver that cannot currently regenerate its own three-dimensional output is not a plan.

One further point in the proposal's favor that it undersells: it correctly notes that GS21.m lines 14-16 declare Epstein-Zin parameters (beta, varphi = 2, gamma = 10) that are NEVER USED -- the SDF is an exogenous lognormal with a constant price of risk gamma_x = 0.5 (line 28). If the paper implies the SDF is derived from preferences, that must be corrected regardless of this proposal.
verdicts.would_it_actually_produce_the_gap: The strongest adversarial case is the same as against Proposal 1 and it applies with more force here. Two priced factors with N = 1000 is still exact factor pricing: mu = B lambda with B of rank 2. The linear span has seven portfolios to hit two exposure targets, and beta_s = G/P >= 0 for every firm means the equal-weight market column already loads on the credit factor. The project's own span2.py measured that under exact factor pricing every basis including equal-weight sits within 0.6% of SR*, and that adding a 20x spread in d does not change this. Raising the priced rank from 1 to 2 does not escape that result -- it is still exact factor pricing, just with K = 2. What produced the 8.6x and 21x oracle ratios in span2.py was an ALPHA: expected return NOT proportional to the covariance loadings. None of the six proposals here, including this one, introduces one, because all six keep a single representative-agent SDF under which mu is minus the covariance with m by construction. That is the deepest gap in the entire proposal set.
verdicts.salvage: Before any MATLAB work: compute the oracle span ratio SR_rff/SR_lin under a REDUCED-FORM two-factor version -- take the existing cond_var and rp from the moments pickle, add a synthetic second loading beta_s proportional to (P_up - P_down)/P_ex at the chosen amplitude and price of risk, and recompute the population span fractions. That is an afternoon's work with objects already on disk and it settles points (a) and the exact-factor-pricing objection without a re-solve. If the oracle ratio clears 2.0, the 64 GB problem becomes worth solving (via the Kronecker structure already present at GS21.m:75-76, or a Python port). If it does not clear 1.5, this proposal and Proposal 1 are both refuted and the model needs an alpha, not another beta.

missed_ideas: THE SENTENCE THAT KILLS THE PAPER, AND NO PROPOSAL ADDRESSES IT: the GS21.m in the replication package cannot regenerate the solution files in the replication package. I verified GS21.m:25 uses sigma_z = 0.16*sqrt((1-0.9^(2/3))/(1-0.9^2)) = 0.0956 with no 0.1 factor, GS21.m:35 uses xi = 0.03/3*3 = 0.03, and GS21.m:27 uses r = 0.1/12; config.py:290/296/299 use 0.014034, 0.01 and 0.074830/12; and the shipped zgrid.max() = 0.146826069677159 matches a THIRD parameterization (0.1*0.16 with the (2/3) exponent) to 15 digits, while xgrid.max() = 0.153723027652884 matches 0.012*sqrt((1-0.95^(2/3))/(1-0.95^2)). GS21.m also calls tauchen and gaussHermite, neither of which exists anywhere in either repository. My report would open: 'The value function on which every result in Section 5 depends cannot be reproduced by anyone, including the authors.' Fix this before considering any economics. Every re-solve proposal (1, 3, 4, 5, 6) is otherwise unimplementable.

THE FAIRNESS DEFECT IS ORTHOGONAL TO ALL SIX PROPOSALS AND WILL BE BLAMED FOR WHATEVER GAP THEY PRODUCE. config.py:187 gives FF and FM ALPHA_LST_FAMA = [0] -- unpenalized OLS, one cell, no tuning. DKKM gets 4 nfeatures x 6 alphas = 24 cells, and create_slides_tables.find_best_alpha_for_model (lines 81-97) selects the alpha by argmax of the mean Sharpe (or argmin HJD) computed ON THE EVALUATION SAMPLE, then reports that cell. Worse, config.py:190 defines ALPHA_LST_GS = [x/100 for x in ALPHA_LST] -- the penalty grid was hand-recentered for GS21, for DKKM only. A referee reads 'we divided the complex model's penalty grid by 100 for this model' as a tuning decision that the benchmarks did not receive. Before any model change: give FF and FM the same ridge grid, run the alpha selection on a held-out split rather than the evaluation metric, and report the full 24-cell DKKM grid rather than its maximum. If DKKM/FF moves off 1.15 under that reform alone, the paper's premise is different from what the authors think it is.

NOBODY PROPOSED THE CHEAPEST AIPT INGREDIENT: MEASUREMENT ERROR AND REPORTING LAGS ON THE EXISTING CHARACTERISTICS. The diagnosis identified as a blocker that GS21's chars invert the state exactly -- bm = 1/P_ex to machine precision, roe is a monotone transform of lagged z, size = log k + log P_ex -- and that an MLP recovers 98.3% of the true SDF weight from them. Real Compustat data forces the opposite: book equity is annual, used for twelve months, reported with a lag, and restated. Simply replacing the monthly book value in panel_functions_gs21.py with a value stale-dated 6 months and updated annually, and adding modest noise to roe, destroys the exact invertibility at zero re-solve cost, zero new economic parameters, and with a defense a referee cannot argue with ('we impose the data-availability convention of Fama-French (1993)'). It is more defensible than every proposal here except the bug fixes and it was not proposed.

NO PROPOSAL INTRODUCES AN UNSPANNED PREMIUM (AN ALPHA), WHICH THE PROJECT'S OWN EVIDENCE SAYS IS THE ONLY THING THAT MATTERS. span2.py measured the RFF-over-linear oracle ceiling at 0.994 under exact factor pricing and 8.6x-21x once expected returns contain a component not proportional to the covariance loadings. All six proposals keep a single representative-agent lognormal SDF (GS21.m:138) under which mu = -cov(m, R) by construction, so alpha is identically zero and the span ceiling is pinned near 1.00 up to O(1/N). Proposals 1 and 6 add differently-shaped BETAS, which does not escape this: with K = 2 and seven linear portfolios the exposure problem is over-determined, and since beta_credit = G/P >= 0 for every firm the equal-weight market column already carries the exposure. The missing option is a segmented-investor or heterogeneous-SDF version of GS21 -- e.g. two investor clienteles with different gamma_x facing a participation constraint, so the marginal investor differs across the cross-section and the observed price reflects a wedge that is a nonlinear function of characteristics. That is harder to defend to a referee than any proposal here, but it is the only one that targets the binding constraint.

NMAT = 5 IS A LOCAL DEVIATION THAT PROVABLY FLATTENS THE COMPLEXITY CURVE, AND FIXING IT IS FREE. config.py:177 says 'ROOT: main_revised.py line 12: nmat = 1' and then sets NMAT = 5. estimate_sdf_dkkm.py averages the stock weights across 5 independent W draws, which converges to kernel ridge at the SAME explicit penalty, cancels exactly the draw-specific high-frequency directions, and makes the large-M limit depend on P only through a vanishing implicit ridge -- i.e. it mechanically flattens Sharpe-versus-nfeatures, which is the curve the paper needs to be rising. Set NMAT = 1 and report the 5 draws as replications. This should be done before any model change, because it is free, it is defensible, and if the flat curve persists at NMAT = 1 that is important information about the models rather than the estimator.

THE HEADLINE OBJECT IS MISSING FROM EVERY TABLE AND EVERY PROPOSAL. max_sr is computed in sdf_compute_gs21.py:222-224 and saved into the moments pickle, but evaluate_sdfs.py never propagates it into results.pkl. Since Sharpe_t(w) = SR*_t x cos_Sigma(w, w*_t) exactly, a table of raw Sharpes is uninterpretable: 0.4433 could be 15% or 95% of the attainable ceiling. Every table must report Sharpe / SR*. This matters especially for Proposal 3, which is predicted to CUT max_sr from 0.438 to 0.15-0.25 per month -- without the normalization, that change looks like every method got worse.

DEMAND THE PLACEBO AT THE NEW CALIBRATION. The diagnosis found that 150 RANDOM Gaussian directions carrying zero characteristic information already attain 0.74-0.82 of GS21's max SR^2, and 90 attain 0.44-0.52. Much of what looks like an RFF span advantage is dimension counting. Any post-change claim that RFF360 attains 0.85-0.95 of max SR^2 must be accompanied by the same number for 360 random directions. If the gap between informed RFF and random RFF is small, the result is plumbing.

REPORT EVERYTHING AT N = 250 / 500 / 1000 / 2000. GS21's maximum Sharpe is 89-97% a cross-sectional alpha leg that scales as sqrt(N) -- a synthetic near-arbitrage with no real-data counterpart. If the DKKM-over-FM gap grows with N, it is a diversification artifact of the simulation design, not a pricing result. This is a one-line experiment and it is the first robustness check I would demand of any positive result. No proposal mentions it.

THE HONEST ALTERNATIVE PAPER WAS NOT CONSIDERED. The current diagnosis is a coherent, publishable negative result: three canonical structural asset pricing models with 1-2 priced aggregate shocks and exact factor pricing cannot generate the virtue of complexity, and here are the five conditions (C1-C5) that a model would have to satisfy. That paper is defensible, cannot be accused of specification search, and is more useful to the literature than a paper that reports a 2x DKKM gap obtained after changing sigma_z, rho_z, tau, kappa_b, kappa_e, bmax, sigma_m, adding zeta(x), five volatility types, and a second priced shock. If the authors proceed with the modifications, they should pre-register the full change list and the target metric before running the pipeline, and publish both the negative baseline and the modified result side by side.

PLUMBING-VERSUS-ECONOMICS RANKING, WHICH IS HOW A REFEREE WILL SORT THESE. Mostly economics: Proposal 5 (turning on frictions the model already contains, at literature-standard values) and Proposal 3's sigma_z restoration (a revert of an undisclosed ad hoc change). Mixed: Proposal 6 (real economics, but gamma_s is free and the effect requires stacking four other changes) and Proposal 1 (real economics in zeta(x), but bundled with a 5x kappa_b move and resting on a span argument I believe is wrong). Mostly plumbing: Proposal 4, whose cleanest claimed DKKM advantage is that FM is denied a ridge penalty (config.py:187), and Proposal 2, which is a necessary bug fix but whose stated DKKM benefit is an effective-rank increase from 20.7 to 38.5 against T = 360 -- a move within the classical regime, not into the one DKKM's theory describes.
